Recent work supports combining textual content with sequential signals, but does not establish that a lightweight text encoder trained from scratch improves BERT4Rec under this benchmark. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines BERT-derived titles, descriptions and reviews with a SASRec-based encoder; its reported Amazon improvements therefore involve a different backbone and unavailable review inputs. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) argues that simple addition of text and ID embeddings can be ineffective because their representations differ, motivating contextual fusion. These findings support testing learned content integration, without assuming semantic similarity implies purchase compatibility.

For timestamps, [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings in self-attention, plus contrastive learning across temporally proximate interactions; it reports gains on its benchmarks. A constraint-compatible experimental hypothesis is one BERT4Rec per category with a small, randomly initialized title/description token encoder, gated content–ID integration, and learned bucketed historical time-gap attention biases, all jointly optimized through masked-item prediction. Preserve reserved-mask inference and final nonpadding readout; exclude target text and unknown target timestamps from inputs. This adaptation is an inference from related work, not a published result for the supplied setting. Ablate content and time separately using macro validation HR@10; no verified 2026 evidence found here establishes the exact proposed combination.
